en: I worship the state of Rāmacandra, which is the absolute liberation beyond the body, whose physical form is composed of the letters beginning with 'a' and ending with 'kṣa', as represented by the rosary.
Oṃ! May my speech be established in my mind; may my mind be established in my speech; be manifest and clear to me.
Be the guardians of my Veda; may what I have heard not be lost to me. By means of this studied [Veda], I join together the days and nights. I shall speak the Ṛta; I shall speak the truth.
May that protect me; may it protect the speaker; may it protect me; may it protect the speaker; may it protect the speaker.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!
Hari Oṃ! Now Prajāpati asked Guha: "O Brahman, tell me the procedure for the classification of the rosary (akṣamālā).

What are its characteristics? How many varieties does it have? How many threads are there? What is the method of construction? What are the colors? What is the consecration (pratiṣṭhā)? Who is its presiding deity? And what is the fruit [of its use]?"

Guha replied to him: "There are coral, pearls, crystal, conch, silver, gold (aṣṭāpada), sandalwood, putrajīvika, and lotuses; these are the rudrākṣas. Their form consists of the letters from 'a' to 'kṣa'; they should be worn with a state of focused awareness. One should join the golden, silver, and copper [beads] such that the mouth [of the bead] faces the mouth [of the next], the tail faces the tail, and they are arranged in the sequence of their internal rotation."
That which is its central thread is Brahman;
that on the right side is Śaiva;
and that on the left is Vaiṣṇava.
That which is its mouth is Sarasvatī; that which is its tail is Gāyatrī;
that which is its hollow is Vidyā.
That which is the knot is *prakṛti*;
those which are the vowels are white;
those which are the consonants are yellow.
Those which are cast away are red.

Then, having purified it with the five fragrances, the five nectars (*amṛta*), and the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), and having bathed it with the five products of the cow and scented water, one should bathe it from that [water] with the syllable *oṃ* using a leaf-bundle (*kūrca*).

Having anointed it with the eight fragrances and placed it upon a bed of flowers, and having worshipped it with unbroken rice and flowers, one should meditate upon it as being directly present through the phonemes beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣa*.
Oṃ! O Aṅkāra, conqueror of death, all-pervading one, be established in the first bead.
Oṃ! O Āṅkāra, whose nature is attraction, omnipresent one, be established in the second bead. Oṃ! O Iṅkāra, bestower of nourishment, agitator of the senses, be established in the third bead.

Oṃ! Oṃ-kāra, the purifier of speech and stainless one, abide in the fourth bead! Oṃ! Oṃ-kāra, the bestower of all strength and most essential, abide in the fifth bead! Oṃ! Oṃ-kāra, the irresistible dispeller [of obstacles], abide in the sixth bead!
Oṃ ṛṅkāra, you who cause agitation and are fickle, abide in the seventh syllable!
Oṃ ṝṅkāra, you who cause delusion and are impetuous, abide in the eighth syllable! Oṃ lṛṅkāra, you who cause hatred and bewilderment, abide in the ninth syllable!
Oṃ *ṛṃ*! O you who cause delusion, abide in the tenth bead.

Oṃ *eṃ*! O you who bring all under control, O you of pure being (*śuddhasattva*), abide in the eleventh bead. Oṃ *aiṃ*! O you who are purely sattvic, O you who bring men under control, abide in the twelfth bead.
Oṃ! O Aṅkāra, you who comprise the entirety of speech and are eternally pure, abide in the thirteenth bead.

Oṃ! O Aṅkāra, you who comprise all speech and bring others under control, abide in the fourteenth bead. Oṃ! O Aṅkāra, you who bring elephants and other beings under control and are the enchanting one, abide in the fifteenth bead.

Oṃ! Oṃ-kāra, destroyer of death, fierce one, abide in the sixteenth bead! Oṃ! Kaṃ-kāra, remover of all poisons, bestower of auspiciousness, abide in the seventeenth bead! Oṃ! Khaṃ-kāra, agitator of all, pervasive one, abide in the eighteenth bead!

Oṃ Gaṅkāra, pacifier of all obstacles, abide in the nineteenth bead! Oṃ Ghaṅkāra, bestower of good fortune and performer of the rite of immobilization, abide in the twentieth bead! Oṃ Ṅakāra, fierce destroyer of all poisons, abide in the twenty-first bead!

Oṃ! Caṃ-kāra, destroyer of malevolent spells, O fierce one, be established in the twenty-second bead! Oṃ! Chaṃ-kāra, creator of the destruction of spirits, O terrifying one, be established in the twenty-third bead!
Oṃ! Jaṃ-kāra, destroyer of sorcery and the like, O invincible one, be established in the twenty-fourth bead!

Oṃ Jhaṅkāra, destroyer of spirits, be established in the twenty-fifth bead! Oṃ Ñakāra, crusher of death, be established in the twenty-sixth bead! Oṃ Ṭaṅkāra, remover of all diseases, fortunate one, be established in the twenty-seventh bead!

Oṃ ṭhaṅkāra! O you who have the form of the moon, be established in the twenty-eighth bead. Oṃ ḍaṅkāra! O you whose nature is Garuḍa, destroyer of poison, auspicious one, be established in the twenty-ninth bead. Oṃ ḍhaṅkāra! O bestower of all prosperity, fortunate one, be established in the thirtieth bead.

Oṃ! O syllable *ṇaṃ*, bestower of all accomplishments, deluder, abide in the thirty-first bead! Oṃ! O syllable *taṃ*, bestower of the wealth of riches, grain, and so forth, gracious one, abide in the thirty-second bead!
Oṃ! O syllable *thaṃ*, producer of the attainment of Dharma, stainless one, abide in the thirty-third bead!

Oṃ! O syllable DAṂ, you who cause nourishment and increase, O one of pleasing appearance, abide in the thirty-fourth bead! Oṃ! O syllable DHAṂ, O destroyer of poison and fever, O vast one, abide in the thirty-fifth bead!
Oṃ! O syllable NAṂ, O bestower of enjoyment and liberation, O peaceful one, abide in the thirty-sixth bead!
Oṃ, O syllable *paṃ*, destroyer of poison and obstacles, auspicious one, be established in the thirty-seventh bead!
Oṃ, O syllable *phaṃ*, bestower of the supernatural powers such as *aṇimā* and others, you who are the form of light, be established in the thirty-eighth bead!
Oṃ, O syllable *baṃ*, remover of all defects, beautiful one, be established in the thirty-ninth bead!

Oṃ bhaṅkāra! O you who pacify spirits and are terrifying, abide in the fortieth bead! Oṃ maṅkāra! O you who cause delusion to those who harbor enmity, abide in the forty-first bead! Oṃ yaṅkāra! O all-pervading purifier, abide in the forty-second bead!

Oṃ! O syllable *raṃ*, burner, transformed one, abide in the forty-third bead. Oṃ! O syllable *laṃ*, sustainer of the universe, radiant one, abide in the forty-fourth bead. Oṃ! O syllable *vaṃ*, maker of all nourishment, stainless one, abide in the forty-fifth bead.

Oṃ! O Śaṅkāra, bestower of all fruits, pure one, be established in the forty-sixth bead. Oṃ! O Ṣaṅkāra, giver of dharma, artha, and kāma, white one, be established in the forty-seventh bead. Oṃ! O Saṅkāra, cause of all, belonging to all castes, be established in the forty-eighth bead.
Oṃ! O syllable Haṃ, source of all speech, stainless one, abide in the forty-ninth letter.

Oṃ! O syllable Laṃ, bestower of all power, primordial one, abide in the fiftieth letter. Oṃ! O syllable Kṣaṃ, revealer of the supreme and subordinate principles, you whose form is the supreme light, abide in the crest-jewel.

Then he said: "To those gods who dwell upon the earth, obeisance! May the Blessed Ones rejoice for the sake of splendor; may the ancestors rejoice for the sake of splendor for this rosary consisting of knowledge.

Then he said: "To those gods who dwell in the intermediate space, *Oṃ* obeisance! May the Blessed Ones rejoice for the sake of splendor; may the ancestors rejoice for the sake of splendor for this rosary consisting of knowledge."

Then he said: "Salutations to those gods who dwell in heaven; may the Blessed Ones rejoice for the sake of splendor; may the ancestors rejoice for the sake of splendor. Salutations to this rosary made of knowledge. Then he said: "Salutations to those mantras and to those sciences; salutations to them, and salutations to their power, which establishes this [rosary].
Then he said: "Salutations, Om, to those Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra who possess attributes; their virility establishes this [rosary]."

Then he said: "Salutations to those who are the various principles of Sāṅkhya and other systems; follow them, and in case of conflict, accommodate them. Then he said: "Salutations, salutations to the Śaivas, Vaiṣṇavas, and Śāktas by the hundreds of thousands; may the Blessed Ones rejoice in this and grant their grace. Then he said: "And to those who possess life-breath within death, salutations, salutations; through this, protect him, protect him!"

Furthermore, having meditated upon her as being the self of all, and having first generated the *ālikā* through contemplation, one should begin by offering that which consists of her with great offerings; then, one should touch the rosary one hundred and eight times with the letters from *a* to *kṣa*.

Then, having raised it once more and circumambulated it, [he should say]: "Oṃ, obeisance to you, O Blessed One, Mother of Mantras, Rosary of Akṣas, who brings all under control! Oṃ, obeisance to you, O Blessed One, Mother of Mantras, Rosary of Akṣas, who paralyzes the remainder! Oṃ, obeisance to you, O Blessed One, Mother of Mantras, Rosary of Akṣas, who causes expulsion! Oṃ, obeisance to you, O Blessed One, Mother of Mantras, Rosary of Akṣas, who is the immortality of the universe, whose very nature is the Conqueror of Death, the illuminator of all worlds, the supreme protector of all worlds, the reviver of all worlds, and the progenitor of all worlds!"

O you who manifest by day, O you who manifest by night; you go to another river, you go to another land, you go to another island, you go to another world; you always throb within every heart and dwell therein. Salutations to you, O supreme form! Salutations to you, O form of *paśyantī*! Salutations to you, O form of *madhyamā*! Salutations to you, O form of *vaikharī*! You whose essence is all principles (*tattva*), whose essence is all knowledge (*vidyā*), whose essence is all powers (*śakti*), whose essence is all gods! You who were worshipped by the sage Vasiṣṭha and upon whom the sage Viśvāmitra depends for his livelihood—salutations to you, salutations to you!
One who studies this in the morning destroys the sin committed during the night.
Reciting it in the evening destroys the evil committed during the day;
one who practices this both morning and evening becomes sinless even if previously sinful.
Thus, a mantra recited with a rosary brings about immediate success.
"It is so," said the Blessed One Guha to Prajāpati; thus ends the Upaniṣad.
Oṃ! May my speech be established in my mind; may my mind be established in my speech; be manifest and clear to me.

Be the two poles for me of the Veda; may what I have heard not perish. By this studied [Veda], I join together days and nights. I shall speak the Ṛta; I shall speak the Truth. May that protect me; may it protect the speaker. May it protect me; may it protect the speaker; may it protect the speaker.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!
Hariḥ Oṃ Tat Sat.
Thus ends the Akṣamālikopaniṣad.
